documents.title: USF Guidance for Ethical Generative AI Usage
documents.stance_why: The document sets no rule of its own for coursework: "use of genAI tools within university coursework is at the discretion of the instructor and students are expected to follow course-specific policies." The rest is general principles for all users, so the stance is delegates.
documents.summary: The Provost's Oct 2023 guidance sets seven principles for ethical genAI use (human-centered, responsibility, bias, sourcing, transparency, discipline-specific, data protection). It leaves coursework use to the instructor and tells students to follow course policies.

documents.stance_why: It states "use of genAI tools within university coursework is at the discretion of individual instructors" and "Faculty retain full control over how, or if, AI tools may be used in their course", so it delegates.

notes: Coder A. Only university-layer documents exist (school, computing none-found; course layer deferred). The GenAI at USF University Guidance page repeats the 2023 Provost principles with updates (Copilot replaces Bing Chat Enterprise; adds workforce-readiness and public-chatbot sections), so overlapping units are coded in both documents. The acceptable-use sample permits 'examinations' yet its own example bars AI on unit exams. PDF text has ligature corruption (e.g. 'expectaIons'); anchors avoid it where possible.
